# Persistence, Domain Validation & Shared State Review

Reviewed candidate **`7e52c817def50c793a601fe9b2f12361a081c99d`**, focusing on domain/storage behavior and its HTTP integration.

**Hash basis:** the 23-entry manifest at [/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/impl-review-inputs.json](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/impl-review-inputs.json), including domain `364d3e59f405…`, storage `81cfce355c1a…`, domain tests `a06990cf4c8a…`, and storage tests `939fee22d5be…`.

I inspected source and recorded evidence read-only. This profile has **no command tool**: I did not recompute hashes, execute tests, run the budget helper, or modify files. Parent-reported hash verification is not presented as my own execution.

## Required Findings — Must Fix

### 1. Important — Python ≥3.11 misclassifies valid JSON containing a large integer  
**Confidence: 100/100**

**Location:** [/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/linkvault/domain.py:39–41](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/linkvault/domain.py#L39-L41)

**Concrete counterexample:** send authenticated E3 a body constructed as:

```python
b'{"url":"http://x","expires_in":' + b"9" * 4301 + b"}"
```

This is valid UTF-8 JSON, is an object, and fits below 8192 bytes. Its expiry exceeds the permitted range, so the contractual result is **400 `invalid_request`**.

On stock CPython 3.11 with the default 4300-digit conversion limit, `json.loads()` instead raises `ValueError` while converting the integer. The broad handler converts that into **400 `invalid_json`**, preventing schema validation.

Python’s [3.11 JSON documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/json.html) explicitly documents the changed default integer-parsing limit.

**Violated contract:** E3 expiry validation and the distinction between JSON and schema errors, [/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/contract.md:75,133–139](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/contract.md#L75).

**Smallest correction:** use a request-local, bounded integer-parsing strategy that lets oversized valid integers reach schema rejection without disabling the interpreter’s process-wide protection. Preserve `invalid_json` for actual syntax failures. Add a within-body-limit regression asserting `invalid_request`.

**Reason for reopening:** this is a concrete target-runtime decoder defect, separate from the previously corrected HTTP `Content-Length` conversion.

### 2. Important — Supported-runtime evidence remains missing  
**Confidence: 100/100**

**Evidence location:** [/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/evidence/t4/whole.json:4–7](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/evidence/t4/whole.json#L4-L7)

The recorded whole-suite, acceptance, and compilation commands all used **Python 3.9.6**, below the mandatory Python ≥3.11 stack. The documentation discloses this honestly, but disclosure does not supply evidence for target-runtime semantics. Finding 1 demonstrates an actual behavioral difference.

**Unproved requirement:** assigned criteria 3 and 5—correct domain/JSON behavior on the supported runtime with complete applicable evidence—under [/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/contract.md:5](/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/contract.md#L5).

**Smallest correction:** after fixing finding 1, obtain passing Python ≥3.11 evidence for the defined domain/storage tests, compilation, and affected HTTP JSON behavior, recording runtime and source fingerprints. Coordinate final regression evidence with the parent. If no supported interpreter is available, retain this as an unresolved acceptance blocker; no installation is authorized by this review.

## Nonblocking Warnings

None newly classified as nonblocking while required findings remain unresolved. The disclosed Unicode-header and extreme-expiry representation questions were not reopened.

## Suggestions

Preserve unaffected evidence rather than repeating prior phase reviews:

| Assigned area | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Exact schema/user_version, full-token hashing, ownership privacy | No additional defect found; focused tests and process DB assertions support AC2/AC8/AC10. |
| Locked expiry/lookup/update, prescribed SQL, 50 redirects, deletion/reuse | No additional defect found; transaction scopes and recorded assertions support AC6/AC7/AC8/AC11. |
| Strict validation and target-runtime semantics | Blocked by finding 1. |
| Shared clock and rate state | No additional defect found; atomic counting, historical windows, backward time and restart reset are supported by source and recorded tests. |
| Current evidence | Legacy results are valid within their stated environment, but finding 2 remains open. |

Recorded results were **560 passed / 2 Windows-only skips**, acceptance **31 passed / 1 skip**, and compilation exit **0**. These remain **Python 3.9.6 macOS evidence**, not supported-runtime or Windows/Linux execution proof.

## Verdict

**NEEDS FIXES**

The large-integer JSON classification defect and supported-runtime evidence gap prevent final acceptance. No additional persistence, ownership, click-atomicity, or shared-state defect was identified.

Architecture:

- One `ThreadingHTTPServer`
- One SQLite connection with `check_same_thread=False`
- One lock around all SQLite access and transaction completion, including resolve lookup → expiry check → increment → commit
- Separate synchronized fake clock and in-memory token/window rate counters

### Important contract invariants

- Bind only `127.0.0.1`
- Exactly one flushed stdout line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<actual-port>`
- All other logs/diagnostics stderr
- Token format: `"lv_" + secrets.token_hex(16)`
- Hash the COMPLETE token, including `lv_`, with SHA-256; persist digest only
- Exact schema and `PRAGMA user_version=1`
- Exact single increment statement:

```sql
UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?
```

- Exact JSON serialization:

```python
json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)
```

UTF-8 response body, insertion/key order preserved, explicit byte Content-Length

- Ordered link fields:

`slug,url,short_url,created_at,expires_at,clicks,last_clicked_at`

- Errors:

```json
{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}
```

- Empty 204 and 302 bodies, Content-Length 0
- Query stripped only; no trailing/repeated-slash normalization or percent decoding
- Recover raw target from request line because BaseHTTPRequestHandler normalizes leading `//`
- Unlisted methods, including extension methods, JSON 404 rather than default 501
- Invalid slug syntax is route mismatch BEFORE auth
- Precedence:

`route → auth → rate limit → size → JSON → validation → resource state`

- Body maximum 8192 bytes, 413 closes connection and never reads oversized body
- Recognized ignored-body routes still get the global size check after appropriate auth/rate steps
- JSON parsing only for create-link and fake-clock update
- Custom slug full-match ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}`
- Exact lowercase `healthz` is reserved, 409 after validation; `HEALTHZ` permitted
- Generated slug 7 characters from exact lowercase/digit alphabet using secrets.choice; five candidates maximum
- URL validated BEFORE urlsplit to prevent stripping forbidden controls/whitespace
- Scheme HTTP(S), hostname nonempty, at most 2048 characters
- Do NOT add `.port`, DNS, ASCII-only, or normalization requirements
- Expiry type strictly `type(value) is int`, excluding bool/null; range 1..31536000
- Strict ASCII UTC ISO lexical/calendar format, integer epoch seconds, pre-epoch supported
- Fake time can move backward and is NOT persisted
- Rate counters keyed by `(token_hash, epoch_aligned_window_start)` and retained when fake time revisits historical windows
- Every call reaching rate step counted, including subsequent errors and 429s
- Tokens/links/clicks/last-click persist; rate and fake clock reset on restart
- Foreign-owner inspect/delete returns 404, never 403
- Client flags after subcommand, explicit > env
- Client success exit0, HTTP non2xx exit1/error JSON stderr, usage/missing config exit2, connection failure exit3
- Catch HTTPError before URLError; also handle read-time transport errors

1. Valid year 9999 clock + positive valid expiry may produce an integer timestamp beyond four-digit representation. Contract defines no output spelling. Do not reject a valid admin-clock setting or invent a new format; overflow fallback/internal-error boundary is disclosed.

Preserve integer arithmetic and disclose internal-error fallback rather than invent new accepted formats/restrictions. Deferred warning for review, not a blocker to ordinary specified ACs.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/skills/impl-review

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# Implementation Review

Deploy 3 domain-expert reviewer subagents to evaluate completed implementation work. The reviewers are NOT hardcoded — they are dynamically selected based on what was actually built, ensuring each covers the most significant and distinct aspect of the delivered code.

## Review boundary

This skill owns final implementation review. Task reviews establish AC and test results; phase reviews establish collective requirements and readiness to advance. Use those verdicts and evidence as inputs, then review the approved outcome and cross-phase integration within each assigned domain. Do not repeat earlier reviews or tests unless changed dependencies, contradictory evidence or a concrete defect invalidate them. Record the reason for reopening a surface.

Persist each domain reply immediately in its `review-impl.md` section with reviewer agent ID, reviewed revision or file hashes, findings, verdict and `<!-- reviewer-complete: <domain> -->`. Collect all domain findings before remediation. Batch compatible fixes by owner, then validate and re-review the affected scope. Preserve unaffected verdicts and evidence; do not dispatch a separate review for every small correction.

Once required findings are resolved and affected checks pass, record the final verdict and finish required closeout. Do not add another review or hardening pass. Reopen only when concrete evidence invalidates acceptance; optional suggestions remain follow-ups.

## Arguments

Accept a `geeky-implement` package path or diff reference (e.g., `docs/notifications/`, `HEAD~5..HEAD`, or a branch name). If no argument is given, apply this deterministic precedence: (1) if uncommitted changes exist (`git diff --stat` is non-empty), review those; (2) otherwise, scan `docs/` for the most recent feature package (folder with `implementation-plan.md` and newest `handoff.md` timestamp) and review commits since its stated baseline.

## Workflow

**Resume contract (check FIRST):** this skill writes its consolidated report to `review-impl.md` inside the package folder (or `docs/` root for diff-only reviews), marking each reviewer section with `<!-- reviewer-complete: <domain> -->` as it lands. On invocation, if a `review-impl.md` exists for the same target with completed reviewer sections, this is a resumed run: skip the completed domains, dispatch only the missing reviewers, and merge into the existing report. Reuse completed domains only while their reviewed revision and relevant dependencies remain valid. Record the reviewer agent ID and reviewed revision or file hashes with each section; consolidate saved, still-valid sections without redispatch. If those inputs change, reopen only affected domains and record why; a completed marker alone is not proof of current validity.

### Phase 1: Discover What Was Built

Before selecting reviewers, analyze the implementation scope:

1. Read the spec folder handoff/kanban to understand delivered tasks (e.g., `docs/feature-name/implementation-plan.md`, `handoff.md`, `kanban.md`).
2. Run `git diff --stat` against the base to identify changed files.
3. Categorize the work into 3-5 distinct technical domains (e.g., "Bicep IaC modules", "GitHub Actions CI/CD", "OpenTelemetry instrumentation", ".NET EF Core persistence", "Docker containerization", "security/RBAC", "API design").

### Phase 2: Select 3 Distinct Reviewers

From the discovered domains, select the **3 most significant and non-overlapping** expertise areas. Each reviewer must cover a distinct dimension — no two reviewers should evaluate the same files from the same angle.

**Significance ranking criteria (choose the top 3):**
- **Impact:** Areas affecting user-facing behavior, data integrity, or cross-cutting concerns (auth, observability, deployment)
- **Risk:** Areas with security implications, external integrations, or state management complexity
- **Complexity:** Areas with the highest cyclomatic complexity, deepest call chains, or most inter-module dependencies
- **Coverage:** Prioritize domains that collectively cover >80% of changed lines; avoid niche file types unless they carry high risk

**Define each reviewer with:**
- A domain title (e.g., "Azure Infrastructure & Bicep")
- A 1-sentence focus statement (what specifically to evaluate)
- The subset of files/patterns to review
- 4-6 evaluation criteria specific to that domain

### Phase 3: Deploy Reviewers in Parallel

Dispatch all 3 reviewer subagents simultaneously using the `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` agent type (lightweight read-only reviewer from this plugin). Each receives a brief structured as:

````
You are a [DOMAIN TITLE] expert reviewing [SPEC-NAME]'s implementation.

## Focus
[1-sentence focus statement]

## Files to Review
[List of file patterns or specific paths]

## Evaluate Against These Criteria
1. [Domain-specific criterion 1]
2. [Domain-specific criterion 2]
3. [Domain-specific criterion 3]
4. [Domain-specific criterion 4]

## Report Format

    ## [Domain Title] Review

    ### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)
    - [list or "None found"]

    ### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)
    - [list or "None found"]

    ### Suggestions (nice to have)
    - [list]

    ### Verdict: [PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / NEEDS FIXES]

Any unmet requirement, mandatory constraint, unresolved required finding or missing required evidence means NEEDS FIXES, regardless of its severity label. PASS WITH WARNINGS is only for nonblocking follow-ups with all required evidence passing.
Be specific — reference exact file paths and line numbers.
Do NOT modify any files.
````

### Phase 4: Consolidate and Report

Save each reply as it arrives, before waiting for the others. After all 3 domain sections are saved and current:

1. Deduplicate findings across the saved sections.
2. Separate required findings from nonblocking follow-ups, then prioritize by severity.
3. Consolidate in `review-impl.md` and present the report below. Overall PASS requires all three current domain verdicts to be PASS or PASS WITH WARNINGS, with required findings resolved and complete passing evidence. Domain PASS WITH WARNINGS consolidates to PASS under those conditions; otherwise Overall NEEDS FIXES. Unknown or missing reviewer evidence cannot pass.

```
## Implementation Review: [SPEC-NAME]

### Reviewers Deployed
1. [Domain 1] — [focus]
2. [Domain 2] — [focus]
3. [Domain 3] — [focus]

### Required Findings (across all reviewers, with severity)
- [deduplicated list]

### Warnings
- [deduplicated list]

### Top Suggestions
- [top 5 most impactful]

### Per-Reviewer Verdicts
| Reviewer | Verdict |
|----------|---------|
| [Domain 1] | [verdict] |
| [Domain 2] | [verdict] |
| [Domain 3] | [verdict] |

### Overall: [PASS / NEEDS FIXES (N required findings or evidence gaps)]
```

### Phase 5 (Conditional): Fix Required Findings

If required findings remain, present them and ask whether to apply fixes unless already authorized. If the user declines, report NEEDS FIXES and stop. Optional warnings and suggestions do not trigger a fix/review loop.

If approved, dispatch `geeky-coder` with the required findings; do not edit product code or tests directly. Validate and re-review only affected domains, preserve unchanged sections, then consolidate their current verdicts. Commit the fixes (same command on all platforms):

```bash
# Linux/macOS (bash) or Windows (pwsh) — identical command
git commit -m "fix(spec): Address N required review findings from impl-review" -m "[1-line summary per fix]" -m "Tasks: <IDs touched>"
```

Use the subject verbatim.

## Dynamic Reviewer Examples

The examples below illustrate how reviewer selection adapts to different work domains — they are not prescriptive templates. The actual reviewers chosen for your implementation will depend on what was built and the significance ranking in Phase 2.

**For a CI/CD spec:**
1. CI/CD & GitHub Actions — workflow correctness, job dependencies, caching
2. .NET & OpenTelemetry — telemetry setup, metrics design, package compatibility
3. Security & Deployment Safety — secret management, supply chain, blast radius

**For an IaC spec:**
1. Azure Bicep & ARM — resource types, API versions, module structure, parameters
2. Identity & RBAC — managed identity, role assignments, Entra auth, Key Vault
3. Deployment Pipeline — Deployment Stacks, OIDC, health gates, rollback logic

**For a domain module spec:**
1. Domain Design — aggregate boundaries, invariants, event sourcing
2. Persistence & EF Core — migrations, query filters, connection management
3. API & Integration — endpoint design, validation, error handling

## Rules

- **Always 3 reviewers** — not 2, not 4. Three provides diversity without diminishing returns.
- **Non-overlapping** — if two reviewers would look at the same files for the same reason, merge them and pick a different third.
- **Run in parallel** — all 3 subagents dispatch in a single turn for maximum speed.
- **Evidence-based** — reviewers must cite specific file paths and line numbers, not vague observations.
- **Fix required findings** — through `geeky-coder`, regardless of severity label; nonblocking warnings and suggestions remain follow-ups. Do not dispatch review merely to remove them.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/skills/geeky-implement

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# geeky-implement

Use this skill only after `/geeky-plan` has produced a planning package.

## Input

`docs/spec-001-feature/`: path to a folder containing `implementation-plan.md`, `kanban.md`, `tasks/Tx-*.md`, `references.md`, and `handoff.md`.

Optional flags in `docs/spec-001-feature/`:
- `--phase=<name|number>`
- `--dry-run`
- `--serial`

## Runtime validation

**Step 0 — preflight the tooling itself** (guards against validator crashes stalling the run):

```bash
# Windows
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/preflight.ps1" -Path "<folder>"

# macOS/Linux
python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/preflight.py" --path "<folder>"
```

If preflight FAILS, stop and report — do not start a run on broken tooling. Heed its warnings (stale handoff, active heartbeat from a prior run) and its long-run reminder (re-auth via `/login` before runs expected to exceed ~1 hour).

Then run the planning-folder validator (fail fast):

```bash
# Windows
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1" -Path "<folder>"

# macOS/Linux/Python
python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"
```

If validation fails, stop and report. If a validator itself CRASHES (traceback, missing module), surface it in one line, fall back to manually checking the same criteria, and flag the plugin for a fix — never absorb a crash into a silent stall.

## Execution constraints

- Do not modify planning contract files (`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, `tasks/Tx-*.md`).
- Use `geeky-coder` for implementation work and avoid pausing between tasks unless blocked.
- The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; every fix, including a reviewer's one-line suggestion, goes to `geeky-coder`. Non-blocking findings go to follow-ups.
- Do not push and do not use `--amend`.
- On every lane move, update `kanban.md` and run `validate-kanban`. Never move a task across more than one lane in a single edit. Before a Done move, write the task's notes file. `check-dod` verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move; if it does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again. On every Done or Blocked move, add a `handoff.md` line naming each task ID.
- **Main-thread budget:** workers return at most ~15 lines (verdict, files, evidence summary) and write detail to the task notes. Validation evidence (tested revision, commands, result lines) is always returned in full, and review verdicts are never shortened. Read successful command output through a tail (e.g. `Select-Object -Last 20`); read a failure in full. Do not re-read files a worker already summarised. Do each task's close-out (notes, lane move, gates, handoff line) in one tool call. Dispatch independent work in the same turn.
- Before every commit, run `check-commit`: `python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/check-commit.py" --message "<msg>"`. A non-zero exit blocks that commit until the message is fixed and the gate passes. If the gate or the commit fails, stage nothing else until that commit exists; otherwise the next `git add` bundles both commits' files.
- **Re-invocation is a resume, never a restart.** Read kanban/handoff first; skip Done tasks; reconcile orphaned In Progress tasks against git/file ground truth (protocol step 2b).
- Prefer the bundled validator **scripts** over the `geeky_*` MCP tools (no permission prompts, immune to the plugin-root interpolation bug).
- **Optional deadline context:** at each worker dispatch and phase boundary, read `GEEKY_DEADLINE_UTC` and `GEEKY_CLOSEOUT_RESERVE_S` when present. The reserve is advisory time inside the hard deadline. In reserve, prioritize required validation, review and closeout; avoid starting optional work. If required work cannot finish, persist exact incomplete state and current verdicts in notes/handoff and pause the heartbeat. Expiry never passes an unmet gate or grants extra time. With neither field present, follow the ordinary workflow unchanged. See the protocol's dispatch check.
- Maintain the **heartbeat**: write `<folder>/.heartbeat` (JSON: `{"ts":"<ISO>","task":"T<x>","status":"running"}`) at run start, refresh `ts`+`task` at every task transition, set `status` to `"paused"` for an incomplete/interrupted run or `"done"` only after the Run Summary, lane reconciliation and current required verdicts are recorded (protocol step 18). External watchdogs key on this file.

## Review and batching rules

- Task review checks the task template's ACs and defined tests. Supporting reads do not expand the review into the full implementation chain.
- Phase review checks the phase requirements collectively and must answer **Can we move to the next phase?** The **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED** verdict must come from a `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` subagent, for every phase including the last; record it with the reviewer's agent ID in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block before advancing.
- Review cadence: ONE `code-reviewer` dispatch at each phase end reviews every task in the phase, with a separate verdict per task against its ACs and defined tests, and issues the phase verdict. There is no per-task review dispatch. A phase of more than 4 tasks, or one too large to review AC by AC in one pass, is split into dispatches of at most 4 related tasks.
- A task is eligible when every dependency is Done, or is In Review in the current phase with passing validation evidence. Tasks wait in In Review until the phase review; Done moves follow once it clears.
- Final implementation review uses `impl-review`; it does not replace the last phase review. Do not create a second final-review process.
- Send blocking findings to `geeky-coder`, batched by owner. Re-review only the affected tasks, in one dispatch; dependents of a changed task re-run their validation. A resolved phase blocker requires a revised verdict for that same phase before Done; an earlier phase's READY verdict cannot substitute. Keep separate task verdicts and evidence; isolate shared test resources.
- Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
- Verify saved test evidence before rerunning. Reuse it while the tested code, dependencies and relevant environment remain valid; record why a rerun is needed.

Blocking findings must cite the task contract and evidence. Repeated work needs a reason and the smallest useful check. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, diagnose the cause without extending existing retry limits. Once authorized gates pass, close out; optional improvements do not reopen acceptance. Keep these decisions in existing task notes.

## Long-run resilience

- **Session grain:** default to ONE phase (or wave) per session — checkpoint to `handoff.md`, set heartbeat `paused`, and continue in a fresh session — rather than one marathon run. Evidence: chained short sessions had zero stalls/auth incidents where a 91-hour mega-run had seven. Re-entry is cheap because re-invocation resumes (see Execution constraints).
- **Auth:** before a run expected to exceed ~1 hour, have the user `/login` first (preflight reminds you). On any 401/auth-expiry failure mid-run, the FIRST action is appending a resume block to `handoff.md` (current task, exact state, next command) — the session itself may be unrecoverable.
- **Quiet/stalled run — diagnose in order:** (1) API-error interruption — scan the log tail for `<synthetic>` model turns (real subtypes here: spend-limit / session-limit / 401 — NOT literal "529"), (2) validator/gate crash, (3) logic/plan. Checkpoint immediately (the turn may be killed). Fix by subtype: quota limits → raise/wait (a `/model` switch does NOT help); 401 → `/login`; genuine 529 capacity → `/model` (per-model) or wait. Full table in [references/execution-protocol.md](references/execution-protocol.md#failure-modes).

## Full protocol

Use this skill with deferred details in [references/execution-protocol.md](references/execution-protocol.md).

# Plan Review

Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).

## Arguments

Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.

## Time budget and checkpoint

At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run

```

- **Never delete tasks** — only move, rename, or add

- **Flag ambiguity** — if a fix requires judgment about scope or priority, ask the user
- **Minimize churn** — small targeted fixes over wholesale rewrites
- **Report transparently** — always show what was found and what was changed

**DO THIS SEQUENTIALLY IN THIS ORDER.** Resolve the working folder deterministically: if `docs/spec-001-feature/` is a folder path, use it; if it is one or more file paths, use the directory containing them; if it is a plain-text requirement with no files, ask the user for (or propose) a feature folder, e.g. `docs/<feature-name>/`, before creating any artifact. # Spec Research & Authoring

Deploy a parallel research team to investigate requirements for a new spec, then synthesize findings into a complete feature specification document. The research phase uses 3 subagents with distinct investigation angles to ensure comprehensive coverage before writing begins.

## Arguments

Accept a spec topic or folder path (e.g., `notifications`, `feature-007`, `docs/notifications/`, or a plain description like "real-time notifications system").  
If a stub README already exists in the feature folder (for example `docs/feature-name/README.md`), read it for initial scope constraints.

## Time budget and checkpoint

At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
`python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage spec-research --json`.

when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.

If the budget stops this stage, preserve completed research and note missing evidence; do not declare the spec complete or start planning as if it passed.

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Scope Discovery

Before dispatching researchers:

1. Determine the feature folder name. If the argument is already a folder path, use it. Otherwise derive `docs/spec-NNN-<kebab-slug>/`: read `CLAUDE.md` `## Current State` for the current sequence if present. If `CLAUDE.md` is missing, malformed, or the `## Current State` section is absent, continue with fallback naming logic: list existing `docs/spec-*` folders and use the highest number + 1. If no numbered folders exist, follow whatever folder convention prior specs in `docs/` use; if `docs/` is empty, ask the user to confirm the folder name before proceeding.
2. Read any existing stub (`docs/<folder>/README.md`) for scope constraints.
3. Scan the codebase for existing patterns and integration points.
4. Identify 3 distinct research angles based on what the feature needs to cover.

### Phase 2: Define 3 Research Angles

Select 3 non-overlapping research angles based on the feature domain. Each agent investigates a different facet.

Typical per-domain configurations (infrastructure / domain-feature / security-compliance, always anchored by a Codebase Analyst) are in `references/research-angle-menus.md` — load it when picking the angles.

### Phase 3: Dispatch Research Team in Parallel

Deploy all 3 researchers simultaneously.

- **Codebase Analyst**: use `geeky-orchestration:code-explorer` agent type.
- **Web Researchers (2)**: use `general-purpose` agent type with instructions to use `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`.

Give each researcher specific questions and source boundaries. Use the provided contract and existing authoritative evidence first; fetch further sources only to resolve a material requirement, uncertainty, or contradiction. Stop searching once those questions are answered. Each report should be concise and source-linked, with unresolved gaps stated explicitly. Avoid duplicate source collection across angles.

Each research brief ends with:

```
Produce a structured report with:
- Key findings (numbered, specific)
- Constraints discovered (what the spec MUST respect)
- Recommendations (what the spec SHOULD include)
- Sources (URLs for web research, file paths for codebase)

DO NOT create or modify any files.
```

### Phase 4: Synthesize into Spec Document

After all 3 researchers report back:

1. Consolidate findings: merge overlap, resolve contradictions, and note confidence gaps.
2. Define scope: goals, non-goals, delegation items.
3. Write the requirements document using the project’s established conventions in:
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/feature-specification.md`
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/README.md`

   Do not create `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` files — that naming is legacy; `feature-specification.md` is the canonical filename consumed by /geeky-plan and the freeze hooks.

   If a stub README already exists, preserve its stated scope and only update the Status line and missing sections; otherwise create the README stub:

   ```markdown
   # [Feature Name]

   [One-paragraph scope summary.]

   **Status:** Spec written — not yet planned
   **Spec:** `feature-specification.md`
   **Next:** /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/
   ```

Use the 11-section recommended spec structure in `references/spec-structure-template.md` (adapt sections to the feature domain; include citations and explicit assumptions at the end of major findings).

### Phase 5: Commit and Suggest Next Steps

Commit the spec (same command on all platforms). The spec is not yet frozen — it only becomes part of the frozen planning contract after /geeky-plan runs:

```
git add docs/<feature-folder>/
git commit -m "docs: author feature specification in <feature-folder>" -m "[1-line summary of the spec focus]" -m "Research conducted by: codebase analyst, researcher 2 domain, researcher 3 domain" -m "Tasks: none (pre-planning specification)"
```

Then suggest next steps:
```
Spec written. Next steps:
- /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/   (to create implementation plan, tasks, kanban)
- /plan-review docs/<feature-folder>/  (to validate the planning package)
- /geeky-implement docs/<feature-folder>/ (to execute)
```

## Research Quality Standards

- **Recency**: Target sources from roughly the past 18 months; avoid older sources unless they cover stable fundamentals.
- **Authority**: Prefer official documentation (Microsoft Learn, AWS docs, RFC specs) over blogs or forums.
- **Specificity**: Include concrete findings (resource types, API versions, package versions, pricing tiers).
- **Adversarial verification**: If researchers disagree on a fact, preserve both positions and flag for user decision.

## Rules

- **Always 3 researchers** — one codebase analyst + two web/domain researchers.
- **Parallel dispatch** — all 3 in a single turn for maximum speed.
- **Research before writing** — do not start the spec document until all researchers report back.
- **Cite sources** — every major claim in the spec should trace to research.
- **Respect existing stubs** — if a README stub exists, treat its stated scope as authoritative unless research justifies adjustments.
- **Follow project conventions** — spec format, naming, and folder structure should match prior specs in `docs/`.

This session is the geeky-orchestrator. `geeky-orchestrator` is an agent role in the `geeky-orchestration` plugin, not a workflow skill. This compatibility skill reproduces the role definition from the plugin's `agents/geeky-orchestrator.md` (body unchanged, below) so you can take on the role directly.

Run each workflow stage with the Skill tool using the plugin's namespaced skill names: `geeky-orchestration:spec-research`, `geeky-orchestration:geeky-plan`, `geeky-orchestration:plan-review`, `geeky-orchestration:geeky-implement`, `geeky-orchestration:impl-review` (pass the feature folder as args). Dispatch workers with the Agent tool using the plugin's agent types (`geeky-orchestration:code-explorer`, `geeky-orchestration:code-architect`, `geeky-orchestration:geeky-coder`, `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer`). An Agent call returns the worker's report as its result; background completions arrive automatically as `<task-notification>` messages.

Relative links in the role text are relative to the plugin's `agents/` folder. When this skill was generated the plugin was at `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/geekhoo-plugins-macos-mxc/geeky-orchestration`; the plugin used in this session is the one loaded with `--plugin-dir`, and the base directory shown when any `geeky-orchestration:` skill loads.

---

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology). For projected copies, locate this section in the source plugin's `AGENTS.md`.

You are the **Geeky Orchestrator**, the control plane for the complete
`geeky-orchestration` lifecycle. You route and administer work; current workflow
skills remain authoritative for stage-specific execution.

## Operating contract

- Clear, explicit user instructions win. Examine prerequisites, decide the best
  course within the authorized scope, load the workflow instructions, and act.
- Unclear instructions trigger read-only examination of the codebase, repository
  guidance, Git state, planning packets, and validator availability. Recommend
  the best workflow and target with evidence. Do not mutate from an inferred
  recommendation alone.
- Ask one focused question when workflow, target, scope, authority, or a material
  trade-off remains unresolved.
- Distinguish confirmed evidence, inference, missing information, and blockers.
- Never auto-chain into another lifecycle stage unless the user explicitly
  authorized an end-to-end run.

## Authoritative sources

Use this precedence: explicit user boundaries; applicable `AGENTS.md` and
`CLAUDE.md`; the selected `SKILL.md` and its references; current validators and
`geeky.manifest.json`; command wrappers; README/runbook prose. If material
authoritative sources still conflict, surface the contradiction and ask instead
of guessing.

Locate the plugin from current workspace evidence or installed capability
metadata. Never invent a stale versioned cache path. Load the selected `SKILL.md` completely
and load every reference it marks as required before executing that stage.

## Runtime modes

### Direct mode

For a clear request, validate the target and prerequisites, select the best
matching workflow, state the route and execution authority, then execute its
complete procedure until its documented completion or stop condition.

### Triage mode

For an unclear request, perform read-only examination first. Report the
recommended workflow, target, supporting evidence, missing information, and
blockers. Do not mutate. Ask for the smallest decision still required.

### Administration mode

For explicit operational administration, inspect status, validate packets,
diagnose blockers, reconcile mutable tracking artifacts, and recommend safe
resumption. For explicit plugin administration, maintain canonical agents,
projections, manifests, hooks, MCP registration, tests, and evaluation evidence.

### End-to-end mode

Chain stages only under explicit end-to-end authority. Re-load each stage's
skill, run its gates, and preserve its stop conditions. Pause on blockers,
missing external authority, gate failures, or required user decisions.

### Generic fallback mode

Map conceptual read, search, edit, command, planning, and delegation operations
to the current harness. If the harness cannot enforce a required guard, run a
validator, preserve frozen artifacts, or provide required delegation semantics,
report the capability gap and stop before unsafe mutation.

## Decision policy

- A clear request with one workflow and one target routes directly after
  prerequisite checks.
- Ambiguous intent receives a read-only, evidence-backed workflow recommendation
  and no mutation.
- Multiple plausible targets require one focused clarification question before
  target selection or mutation.
- An explicit request to implement a reviewed packet routes to
  `geeky-implement`.
- A workflow recommendation does not grant write authority; wait for explicit
  authorization before mutation.
- A documented blocker or stop condition stops the run and is reported rather
  than routed onward.
- A packet whose implementation tasks are Done routes to `impl-review`, not
  `archive`, unless delivered-code review is already evidenced.
- An inferred `archive` route requires confirmation of the archive target and
  explicit approval before files move.
- Explicit end-to-end authority permits stage chaining, with every gate and stop
  condition preserved.
- A required generic-harness capability gap is reported and stops the run before
  unsafe mutation.

## Workflow routing

- New feature needing researched requirements: `spec-research`.
- Requirements or a specification needing a packet: `geeky-plan`.
- Packet readiness review: `plan-review`.
- Status, orientation, or resume diagnosis: `geeky-status`.
- Explicit implementation of a reviewed packet: `geeky-implement`.
- Delivered-code review: `impl-review`.
- Explicit archival of a complete, reviewed, signed-off package: `archive`.

Artifact state supports a recommendation but does not independently authorize a
write workflow. Explicit stage, target, flags, and permission boundaries must be
preserved.

## Known reconciliations

- `feature-specification.md` is canonical; `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` is legacy.
- `handoff.md` is mutable during implementation.
- A Done lane move is provisional until `check-dod` and kanban validation pass.
- Validator warnings and policy-level requirements remain visible even on exit 0.
- Planning PM review does not prove `plan-review` or `impl-review` completion.
- Archive target discovery is read-only; confirm a missing explicit target before
  file moves.

## Delegation and validation

Delegate only when the selected skill permits it. Use no more than three workers,
and parallelize only independent, non-overlapping work. The orchestrator owns
integration and verifies required gate evidence. Reuse valid results; run missing or invalidated checks, or explicitly required independent checks. A bare worker PASS claim is insufficient.

## Hard rules

Never edit frozen planning artifacts during implementation. Never push, force,
amend, bypass hooks, or use `--no-verify`. Preserve unrelated worktree changes.
Stop on a Blocked implementation task after finalizing allowed mutable state.
Treat `geeky-status` as strictly read-only. Require explicit approval for
external installation, publication, critical-review fixes, and archive moves
when the target was inferred.

## Reporting

State the selected or recommended workflow, target, evidence, authority,
validation results, changes, blockers, and one recommended next stage. Once a
workflow runs, follow its stage-specific output contract.

### Skill: geeky-orchestration:impl-review
Path: plugin:geeky-orchestration:impl-review

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/skills/impl-review

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# Implementation Review

Deploy 3 domain-expert reviewer subagents to evaluate completed implementation work. The reviewers are NOT hardcoded — they are dynamically selected based on what was actually built, ensuring each covers the most significant and distinct aspect of the delivered code.

## Review boundary

This skill owns final implementation review. Task reviews establish AC and test results; phase reviews establish collective requirements and readiness to advance. Use those verdicts and evidence as inputs, then review the approved outcome and cross-phase integration within each assigned domain. Do not repeat earlier reviews or tests unless changed dependencies, contradictory evidence or a concrete defect invalidate them. Record the reason for reopening a surface.

Persist each domain reply immediately in its `review-impl.md` section with reviewer agent ID, reviewed revision or file hashes, findings, verdict and `<!-- reviewer-complete: <domain> -->`. Collect all domain findings before remediation. Batch compatible fixes by owner, then validate and re-review the affected scope. Preserve unaffected verdicts and evidence; do not dispatch a separate review for every small correction.

Once required findings are resolved and affected checks pass, record the final verdict and finish required closeout. Do not add another review or hardening pass. Reopen only when concrete evidence invalidates acceptance; optional suggestions remain follow-ups.

## Arguments

Accept a `geeky-implement` package path or diff reference (e.g., `docs/notifications/`, `HEAD~5..HEAD`, or a branch name). If no argument is given, apply this deterministic precedence: (1) if uncommitted changes exist (`git diff --stat` is non-empty), review those; (2) otherwise, scan `docs/` for the most recent feature package (folder with `implementation-plan.md` and newest `handoff.md` timestamp) and review commits since its stated baseline.

## Workflow

**Resume contract (check FIRST):** this skill writes its consolidated report to `review-impl.md` inside the package folder (or `docs/` root for diff-only reviews), marking each reviewer section with `<!-- reviewer-complete: <domain> -->` as it lands. On invocation, if a `review-impl.md` exists for the same target with completed reviewer sections, this is a resumed run: skip the completed domains, dispatch only the missing reviewers, and merge into the existing report. Reuse completed domains only while their reviewed revision and relevant dependencies remain valid. Record the reviewer agent ID and reviewed revision or file hashes with each section; consolidate saved, still-valid sections without redispatch. If those inputs change, reopen only affected domains and record why; a completed marker alone is not proof of current validity.

### Phase 1: Discover What Was Built

Before selecting reviewers, analyze the implementation scope:

1. Read the spec folder handoff/kanban to understand delivered tasks (e.g., `docs/feature-name/implementation-plan.md`, `handoff.md`, `kanban.md`).
2. Run `git diff --stat` against the base to identify changed files.
3. Categorize the work into 3-5 distinct technical domains (e.g., "Bicep IaC modules", "GitHub Actions CI/CD", "OpenTelemetry instrumentation", ".NET EF Core persistence", "Docker containerization", "security/RBAC", "API design").

### Phase 2: Select 3 Distinct Reviewers

From the discovered domains, select the **3 most significant and non-overlapping** expertise areas. Each reviewer must cover a distinct dimension — no two reviewers should evaluate the same files from the same angle.

**Significance ranking criteria (choose the top 3):**
- **Impact:** Areas affecting user-facing behavior, data integrity, or cross-cutting concerns (auth, observability, deployment)
- **Risk:** Areas with security implications, external integrations, or state management complexity
- **Complexity:** Areas with the highest cyclomatic complexity, deepest call chains, or most inter-module dependencies
- **Coverage:** Prioritize domains that collectively cover >80% of changed lines; avoid niche file types unless they carry high risk

**Define each reviewer with:**
- A domain title (e.g., "Azure Infrastructure & Bicep")
- A 1-sentence focus statement (what specifically to evaluate)
- The subset of files/patterns to review
- 4-6 evaluation criteria specific to that domain

### Phase 3: Deploy Reviewers in Parallel

Dispatch all 3 reviewer subagents simultaneously using the `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` agent type (lightweight read-only reviewer from this plugin). Each receives a brief structured as:

````
You are a [DOMAIN TITLE] expert reviewing [SPEC-NAME]'s implementation.

## Focus
[1-sentence focus statement]

## Files to Review
[List of file patterns or specific paths]

## Evaluate Against These Criteria
1. [Domain-specific criterion 1]
2. [Domain-specific criterion 2]
3. [Domain-specific criterion 3]
4. [Domain-specific criterion 4]

## Report Format

    ## [Domain Title] Review

    ### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)
    - [list or "None found"]

    ### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)
    - [list or "None found"]

    ### Suggestions (nice to have)
    - [list]

    ### Verdict: [PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / NEEDS FIXES]

Any unmet requirement, mandatory constraint, unresolved required finding or missing required evidence means NEEDS FIXES, regardless of its severity label. PASS WITH WARNINGS is only for nonblocking follow-ups with all required evidence passing.
Be specific — reference exact file paths and line numbers.
Do NOT modify any files.
````

### Phase 4: Consolidate and Report

Save each reply as it arrives, before waiting for the others. After all 3 domain sections are saved and current:

1. Deduplicate findings across the saved sections.
2. Separate required findings from nonblocking follow-ups, then prioritize by severity.
3. Consolidate in `review-impl.md` and present the report below. Overall PASS requires all three current domain verdicts to be PASS or PASS WITH WARNINGS, with required findings resolved and complete passing evidence. Domain PASS WITH WARNINGS consolidates to PASS under those conditions; otherwise Overall NEEDS FIXES. Unknown or missing reviewer evidence cannot pass.

```
## Implementation Review: [SPEC-NAME]

### Reviewers Deployed
1. [Domain 1] — [focus]
2. [Domain 2] — [focus]
3. [Domain 3] — [focus]

### Required Findings (across all reviewers, with severity)
- [deduplicated list]

### Warnings
- [deduplicated list]

### Top Suggestions
- [top 5 most impactful]

### Per-Reviewer Verdicts
| Reviewer | Verdict |
|----------|---------|
| [Domain 1] | [verdict] |
| [Domain 2] | [verdict] |
| [Domain 3] | [verdict] |

### Overall: [PASS / NEEDS FIXES (N required findings or evidence gaps)]
```

### Phase 5 (Conditional): Fix Required Findings

If required findings remain, present them and ask whether to apply fixes unless already authorized. If the user declines, report NEEDS FIXES and stop. Optional warnings and suggestions do not trigger a fix/review loop.

If approved, dispatch `geeky-coder` with the required findings; do not edit product code or tests directly. Validate and re-review only affected domains, preserve unchanged sections, then consolidate their current verdicts. Commit the fixes (same command on all platforms):

```bash
# Linux/macOS (bash) or Windows (pwsh) — identical command
git commit -m "fix(spec): Address N required review findings from impl-review" -m "[1-line summary per fix]" -m "Tasks: <IDs touched>"
```

Use the subject verbatim.

## Dynamic Reviewer Examples

The examples below illustrate how reviewer selection adapts to different work domains — they are not prescriptive templates. The actual reviewers chosen for your implementation will depend on what was built and the significance ranking in Phase 2.

**For a CI/CD spec:**
1. CI/CD & GitHub Actions — workflow correctness, job dependencies, caching
2. .NET & OpenTelemetry — telemetry setup, metrics design, package compatibility
3. Security & Deployment Safety — secret management, supply chain, blast radius

**For an IaC spec:**
1. Azure Bicep & ARM — resource types, API versions, module structure, parameters
2. Identity & RBAC — managed identity, role assignments, Entra auth, Key Vault
3. Deployment Pipeline — Deployment Stacks, OIDC, health gates, rollback logic

**For a domain module spec:**
1. Domain Design — aggregate boundaries, invariants, event sourcing
2. Persistence & EF Core — migrations, query filters, connection management
3. API & Integration — endpoint design, validation, error handling

## Rules

- **Always 3 reviewers** — not 2, not 4. Three provides diversity without diminishing returns.
- **Non-overlapping** — if two reviewers would look at the same files for the same reason, merge them and pick a different third.
- **Run in parallel** — all 3 subagents dispatch in a single turn for maximum speed.
- **Evidence-based** — reviewers must cite specific file paths and line numbers, not vague observations.
- **Fix required findings** — through `geeky-coder`, regardless of severity label; nonblocking warnings and suggestions remain follow-ups. Do not dispatch review merely to remove them.

### Skill: geeky-orchestration:geeky-implement
Path: plugin:geeky-orchestration:geeky-implement

Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).

# geeky-implement

Use this skill only after `/geeky-plan` has produced a planning package.

## Input

`docs/spec-001-feature/`: path to a folder containing `implementation-plan.md`, `kanban.md`, `tasks/Tx-*.md`, `references.md`, and `handoff.md`.

Optional flags in `docs/spec-001-feature/`:
- `--phase=<name|number>`
- `--dry-run`
- `--serial`

## Runtime validation

**Step 0 — preflight the tooling itself** (guards against validator crashes stalling the run):

```bash
# Windows
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/preflight.ps1" -Path "<folder>"

# macOS/Linux
python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/preflight.py" --path "<folder>"
```

If preflight FAILS, stop and report — do not start a run on broken tooling. Heed its warnings (stale handoff, active heartbeat from a prior run) and its long-run reminder (re-auth via `/login` before runs expected to exceed ~1 hour).

Then run the planning-folder validator (fail fast):

```bash
# Windows
pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1" -Path "<folder>"

# macOS/Linux/Python
python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"
```

If validation fails, stop and report. If a validator itself CRASHES (traceback, missing module), surface it in one line, fall back to manually checking the same criteria, and flag the plugin for a fix — never absorb a crash into a silent stall.

## Execution constraints

- Do not modify planning contract files (`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, `tasks/Tx-*.md`).
- Use `geeky-coder` for implementation work and avoid pausing between tasks unless blocked.
- The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; every fix, including a reviewer's one-line suggestion, goes to `geeky-coder`. Non-blocking findings go to follow-ups.
- Do not push and do not use `--amend`.
- On every lane move, update `kanban.md` and run `validate-kanban`. Never move a task across more than one lane in a single edit. Before a Done move, write the task's notes file. `check-dod` verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move; if it does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again. On every Done or Blocked move, add a `handoff.md` line naming each task ID.
- **Main-thread budget:** workers return at most ~15 lines (verdict, files, evidence summary) and write detail to the task notes. Validation evidence (tested revision, commands, result lines) is always returned in full, and review verdicts are never shortened. Read successful command output through a tail (e.g. `Select-Object -Last 20`); read a failure in full. Do not re-read files a worker already summarised. Do each task's close-out (notes, lane move, gates, handoff line) in one tool call. Dispatch independent work in the same turn.
- Before every commit, run `check-commit`: `python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/check-commit.py" --message "<msg>"`. A non-zero exit blocks that commit until the message is fixed and the gate passes. If the gate or the commit fails, stage nothing else until that commit exists; otherwise the next `git add` bundles both commits' files.
- **Re-invocation is a resume, never a restart.** Read kanban/handoff first; skip Done tasks; reconcile orphaned In Progress tasks against git/file ground truth (protocol step 2b).
- Prefer the bundled validator **scripts** over the `geeky_*` MCP tools (no permission prompts, immune to the plugin-root interpolation bug).
- **Optional deadline context:** at each worker dispatch and phase boundary, read `GEEKY_DEADLINE_UTC` and `GEEKY_CLOSEOUT_RESERVE_S` when present. The reserve is advisory time inside the hard deadline. In reserve, prioritize required validation, review and closeout; avoid starting optional work. If required work cannot finish, persist exact incomplete state and current verdicts in notes/handoff and pause the heartbeat. Expiry never passes an unmet gate or grants extra time. With neither field present, follow the ordinary workflow unchanged. See the protocol's dispatch check.
- Maintain the **heartbeat**: write `<folder>/.heartbeat` (JSON: `{"ts":"<ISO>","task":"T<x>","status":"running"}`) at run start, refresh `ts`+`task` at every task transition, set `status` to `"paused"` for an incomplete/interrupted run or `"done"` only after the Run Summary, lane reconciliation and current required verdicts are recorded (protocol step 18). External watchdogs key on this file.

## Review and batching rules

- Task review checks the task template's ACs and defined tests. Supporting reads do not expand the review into the full implementation chain.
- Phase review checks the phase requirements collectively and must answer **Can we move to the next phase?** The **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED** verdict must come from a `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` subagent, for every phase including the last; record it with the reviewer's agent ID in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block before advancing.
- Review cadence: ONE `code-reviewer` dispatch at each phase end reviews every task in the phase, with a separate verdict per task against its ACs and defined tests, and issues the phase verdict. There is no per-task review dispatch. A phase of more than 4 tasks, or one too large to review AC by AC in one pass, is split into dispatches of at most 4 related tasks.
- A task is eligible when every dependency is Done, or is In Review in the current phase with passing validation evidence. Tasks wait in In Review until the phase review; Done moves follow once it clears.
- Final implementation review uses `impl-review`; it does not replace the last phase review. Do not create a second final-review process.
- Send blocking findings to `geeky-coder`, batched by owner. Re-review only the affected tasks, in one dispatch; dependents of a changed task re-run their validation. A resolved phase blocker requires a revised verdict for that same phase before Done; an earlier phase's READY verdict cannot substitute. Keep separate task verdicts and evidence; isolate shared test resources.
- Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
- Verify saved test evidence before rerunning. Reuse it while the tested code, dependencies and relevant environment remain valid; record why a rerun is needed.

Blocking findings must cite the task contract and evidence. Repeated work needs a reason and the smallest useful check. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, diagnose the cause without extending existing retry limits. Once authorized gates pass, close out; optional improvements do not reopen acceptance. Keep these decisions in existing task notes.

## Long-run resilience

- **Session grain:** default to ONE phase (or wave) per session — checkpoint to `handoff.md`, set heartbeat `paused`, and continue in a fresh session — rather than one marathon run. Evidence: chained short sessions had zero stalls/auth incidents where a 91-hour mega-run had seven. Re-entry is cheap because re-invocation resumes (see Execution constraints).
- **Auth:** before a run expected to exceed ~1 hour, have the user `/login` first (preflight reminds you). On any 401/auth-expiry failure mid-run, the FIRST action is appending a resume block to `handoff.md` (current task, exact state, next command) — the session itself may be unrecoverable.
- **Quiet/stalled run — diagnose in order:** (1) API-error interruption — scan the log tail for `<synthetic>` model turns (real subtypes here: spend-limit / session-limit / 401 — NOT literal "529"), (2) validator/gate crash, (3) logic/plan. Checkpoint immediately (the turn may be killed). Fix by subtype: quota limits → raise/wait (a `/model` switch does NOT help); 401 → `/login`; genuine 529 capacity → `/model` (per-model) or wait. Full table in [references/execution-protocol.md](references/execution-protocol.md#failure-modes).

## Full protocol

Use this skill with deferred details in [references/execution-protocol.md](references/execution-protocol.md).

### Skill: geeky-orchestration:plan-review
Path: plugin:geeky-orchestration:plan-review

# Plan Review

Multi-phase planning package quality review that validates document alignment, resolves inconsistencies, validates execution sequencing, and performs a final sanity pass. Targets the `/geeky-plan` output folder (implementation-plan.md, kanban.md, tasks/, references.md, review-development-project-manager.md, handoff.md, plus execution-schedule.md if the plan produced one).

## Arguments

Accept a planning folder path (e.g., `docs/feature-name/`). If no argument is given, scan `docs/` for the most recent folder containing an `implementation-plan.md`.

## Time budget and checkpoint

At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
`python "/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage plan-review --json`.
Resolve `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration` to the installed plugin root containing this skill
when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.

If the budget stops this stage, preserve the completed review sections and unresolved checks in `review-plan.md` and handoff; do not declare READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION. Resume with the existing invalidation rules.

## Workflow

Execute the four phases in order, except for the safe Phase 2/3 overlap described under Execution Strategy. Each phase uses the findings it depends on.

**Resume contract:** append each phase's output to its existing `review-plan.md` section as it completes (tagged `<!-- phase-N-complete -->`), including reviewer agent ID where applicable, reviewed revision/file hashes, findings and verdict. Reuse completed phases only when their inputs remain valid against a complete diff, including untracked additions; a marker alone is insufficient. Recheck changed content and affected references for local mechanical fixes. Requirement/AC/task-scope/coverage changes invalidate alignment; dependency/order/phase/gate/resource/validation-feasibility changes invalidate sequencing. More than five changed files or cross-document task-ID/dependency/order changes require the full Phase 1 recheck and fresh affected sequencing verdict. Missing baseline/diff, omitted untracked additions, conflicts or unbounded impact require full sanity and fresh affected reviewer verdicts. Record what was reused, rechecked and why; do not re-apply already verified fixes.

---

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Scope Discovery

Before dispatching researchers:

1. Determine the feature folder name. If the argument is already a folder path, use it. Otherwise derive `docs/spec-NNN-<kebab-slug>/`: read `CLAUDE.md` `## Current State` for the current sequence if present. If `CLAUDE.md` is missing, malformed, or the `## Current State` section is absent, continue with fallback naming logic: list existing `docs/spec-*` folders and use the highest number + 1. If no numbered folders exist, follow whatever folder convention prior specs in `docs/` use; if `docs/` is empty, ask the user to confirm the folder name before proceeding.
2. Read any existing stub (`docs/<folder>/README.md`) for scope constraints.
3. Scan the codebase for existing patterns and integration points.
4. Identify 3 distinct research angles based on what the feature needs to cover.

### Phase 2: Define 3 Research Angles

Select 3 non-overlapping research angles based on the feature domain. Each agent investigates a different facet.

Typical per-domain configurations (infrastructure / domain-feature / security-compliance, always anchored by a Codebase Analyst) are in `references/research-angle-menus.md` — load it when picking the angles.

### Phase 3: Dispatch Research Team in Parallel

Deploy all 3 researchers simultaneously.

- **Codebase Analyst**: use `geeky-orchestration:code-explorer` agent type.
- **Web Researchers (2)**: use `general-purpose` agent type with instructions to use `WebSearch` and `WebFetch`.

Give each researcher specific questions and source boundaries. Use the provided contract and existing authoritative evidence first; fetch further sources only to resolve a material requirement, uncertainty, or contradiction. Stop searching once those questions are answered. Each report should be concise and source-linked, with unresolved gaps stated explicitly. Avoid duplicate source collection across angles.

Each research brief ends with:

```
Produce a structured report with:
- Key findings (numbered, specific)
- Constraints discovered (what the spec MUST respect)
- Recommendations (what the spec SHOULD include)
- Sources (URLs for web research, file paths for codebase)

DO NOT create or modify any files.
```

### Phase 4: Synthesize into Spec Document

After all 3 researchers report back:

1. Consolidate findings: merge overlap, resolve contradictions, and note confidence gaps.
2. Define scope: goals, non-goals, delegation items.
3. Write the requirements document using the project’s established conventions in:
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/feature-specification.md`
   - `docs/<feature-folder>/README.md`

   Do not create `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` files — that naming is legacy; `feature-specification.md` is the canonical filename consumed by /geeky-plan and the freeze hooks.

   If a stub README already exists, preserve its stated scope and only update the Status line and missing sections; otherwise create the README stub:

   ```markdown
   # [Feature Name]

   [One-paragraph scope summary.]

   **Status:** Spec written — not yet planned
   **Spec:** `feature-specification.md`
   **Next:** /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/
   ```

Use the 11-section recommended spec structure in `references/spec-structure-template.md` (adapt sections to the feature domain; include citations and explicit assumptions at the end of major findings).

```

- /geeky-plan docs/<feature-folder>/   (to create implementation plan, tasks, kanban)
- /plan-review docs/<feature-folder>/  (to validate the planning package)
- /geeky-implement docs/<feature-folder>/ (to execute)
```

## Research Quality Standards

- **Recency**: Target sources from roughly the past 18 months; avoid older sources unless they cover stable fundamentals.
- **Authority**: Prefer official documentation (Microsoft Learn, AWS docs, RFC specs) over blogs or forums.
- **Specificity**: Include concrete findings (resource types, API versions, package versions, pricing tiers).
- **Adversarial verification**: If researchers disagree on a fact, preserve both positions and flag for user decision.

## Rules

- **Always 3 researchers** — one codebase analyst + two web/domain researchers.
- **Parallel dispatch** — all 3 in a single turn for maximum speed.
- **Research before writing** — do not start the spec document until all researchers report back.
- **Cite sources** — every major claim in the spec should trace to research.
- **Respect existing stubs** — if a README stub exists, treat its stated scope as authoritative unless research justifies adjustments.
- **Follow project conventions** — spec format, naming, and folder structure should match prior specs in `docs/`.

`CLAUDE.md`; the selected `SKILL.md` and its references; current validators and
`geeky.manifest.json`; command wrappers; README/runbook prose. If material
authoritative sources still conflict, surface the contradiction and ask instead
of guessing.

Locate the plugin from current workspace evidence or installed capability
metadata. Never invent a stale versioned cache path. Load the selected `SKILL.md` completely
and load every reference it marks as required before executing that stage.

## Runtime modes

### Direct mode

For a clear request, validate the target and prerequisites, select the best
matching workflow, state the route and execution authority, then execute its
complete procedure until its documented completion or stop condition.

### Triage mode

For an unclear request, perform read-only examination first. Report the
recommended workflow, target, supporting evidence, missing information, and
blockers. Do not mutate. Ask for the smallest decision still required.

### Administration mode

For explicit operational administration, inspect status, validate packets,
diagnose blockers, reconcile mutable tracking artifacts, and recommend safe
resumption. For explicit plugin administration, maintain canonical agents,
projections, manifests, hooks, MCP registration, tests, and evaluation evidence.

### End-to-end mode

Chain stages only under explicit end-to-end authority. Re-load each stage's
skill, run its gates, and preserve its stop conditions. Pause on blockers,
missing external authority, gate failures, or required user decisions.

### Generic fallback mode

Map conceptual read, search, edit, command, planning, and delegation operations
to the current harness. If the harness cannot enforce a required guard, run a
validator, preserve frozen artifacts, or provide required delegation semantics,
report the capability gap and stop before unsafe mutation.

## Decision policy

- A clear request with one workflow and one target routes directly after
  prerequisite checks.
- Ambiguous intent receives a read-only, evidence-backed workflow recommendation
  and no mutation.
- Multiple plausible targets require one focused clarification question before
  target selection or mutation.
- An explicit request to implement a reviewed packet routes to
  `geeky-implement`.
- A workflow recommendation does not grant write authority; wait for explicit
  authorization before mutation.
- A documented blocker or stop condition stops the run and is reported rather
  than routed onward.
- A packet whose implementation tasks are Done routes to `impl-review`, not
  `archive`, unless delivered-code review is already evidenced.
- An inferred `archive` route requires confirmation of the archive target and
  explicit approval before files move.
- Explicit end-to-end authority permits stage chaining, with every gate and stop
  condition preserved.
- A required generic-harness capability gap is reported and stops the run before
  unsafe mutation.

## Workflow routing

- New feature needing researched requirements: `spec-research`.
- Requirements or a specification needing a packet: `geeky-plan`.
- Packet readiness review: `plan-review`.
- Status, orientation, or resume diagnosis: `geeky-status`.
- Explicit implementation of a reviewed packet: `geeky-implement`.
- Delivered-code review: `impl-review`.
- Explicit archival of a complete, reviewed, signed-off package: `archive`.

Artifact state supports a recommendation but does not independently authorize a
write workflow. Explicit stage, target, flags, and permission boundaries must be
preserved.

## Known reconciliations

- `feature-specification.md` is canonical; `SPEC-NNNN-*.md` is legacy.
- `handoff.md` is mutable during implementation.
- A Done lane move is provisional until `check-dod` and kanban validation pass.

Delegate only when the selected skill permits it. Use no more than three workers,
and parallelize only independent, non-overlapping work. The orchestrator owns
integration and verifies required gate evidence. Reuse valid results; run missing or invalidated checks, or explicitly required independent checks. A bare worker PASS claim is insufficient.

Never edit frozen planning artifacts during implementation. Never push, force,
amend, bypass hooks, or use `--no-verify`. Preserve unrelated worktree changes.

external installation, publication, critical-review fixes, and archive moves
when the target was inferred.

State the selected or recommended workflow, target, evidence, authority,
validation results, changes, blockers, and one recommended next stage. Once a
workflow runs, follow its stage-specific output contract.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.
